title: Isaiah, Chapter 55 (Great Isaiah Scroll, 1QIsa-a)
source: Great Isaiah Scroll 1QIsa-a: Israel Museum / Google Art Project photograph (Wikimedia Commons, PD) + ETCBC dss transcription (Abegg; CC BY-NC 4.0) + KJV (bible-api.com)
description: Isaiah 55 as written in the Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a, c. 125 BCE, Qumran Cave 1, Israel Museum), shown with the specific scroll column(s) 45, 46 that carry each section. Hebrew is the scroll's own transcription (ETCBC dss / Abegg), not the Masoretic text; English is the King James Version.
introduction:
Isaiah 55 from the Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsaa), the complete copy of Isaiah found in Cave 1 at Qumran in 1947 and now in the Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem. Copied around 125 BCE, it is roughly a thousand years older than the Leningrad Codex, the oldest complete Masoretic manuscript. This chapter stands in col. XLV (45), col. XLVI (46) of the scroll's 54 columns.

  1. Scan: each section is shown with the actual column of the scroll that carries it, cropped from the Israel Museum / Google Art Project photograph of the whole scroll published on Wikimedia Commons (public domain). The column for every verse comes from the transcription itself, which records the column and line of each word.
  2. Hebrew: the scroll's own text, verbatim from the ETCBC dss Text-Fabric dataset (Jacobs, Naaijer and Roorda, from Martin G. Abegg Jr.'s transcription; CC BY-NC 4.0). This is not the Masoretic text: 1QIsaa uses a fuller spelling (for example לוא for לא, כיא for כי) and differs from the Masoretic text in a number of readings. No vowel points exist in the scroll and none are added. Marks: ⟨x⟩ letters the scribe added above the line, [x] modern reconstruction of text lost to damage, {{x}} letters cancelled by an ancient scribe, ⟪x⟫ an ancient correction, a dot under a letter (x̣) an uncertain reading, ···· four dots written in place of the divine name (Tetrapuncta).
  3. English: the King James Version (1611, public domain), verbatim from bible-api.com. The KJV translates the Masoretic text, so where the scroll reads differently the English will not match the Hebrew shown; the scroll's reading can be checked on the column image.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>הוי כול צמא לכו למים ואשר אין לו כסף לכו שבורו בלוא כסף ובלוא מחיר יין וחלב <sup>2</sup>למה תשקולו כסף בלוא לחם ויגיעכ̣ם בלוא שבעה שמעו שמעוא אלי ואכולו טוב ותתענג בדשן נפשכם <sup>3</sup>הטו אוזנכמה ולכו אלי ושמעו ותחי{{ה}} נפשכםה ואכרות לכמה ברית עולם חסדי דויד הנאמנים <sup>4</sup>הנה עד לאומים נתתיהו נגיד ומצוה לאומים <sup>5</sup>הנה גוי לוא תדע תקרא וגוי לוא ידעכה אליכה ירוץ למען יהוה אלוהיך ו⟨ל⟩קדוש ישראל כיא פארך <sup>6</sup>דרושו יהוה בהמצאו קראוהי בהיותו קרוב <sup>7</sup>יעזב רשע דרכו ואיש און מחשבותיו וישוב אל יהוה וירחמהו ואל אלוהינו כיא ירבה לסלוח
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price. <sup>2</sup>Wherefore do ye spend money for that which is not bread? and your labour for that which satisfieth not? hearken diligently unto me, and eat ye that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in fatness. <sup>3</sup>Incline your ear, and come unto me: hear, and your soul shall live; and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David. <sup>4</sup>Behold, I have given him for a witness to the people, a leader and commander to the people. <sup>5</sup>Behold, thou shalt call a nation that thou knowest not, and nations that knew not thee shall run unto thee because of the LORD thy God, and for the Holy One of Israel; for he hath glorified thee. <sup>6</sup>Seek ye the LORD while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near: <sup>7</sup>Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the LORD, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.

translation.original_ref: Isaiah 55:8-13 (1QIsa-a col. XLV line 28; col. XLVI lines 1-9)
translation.original_text: <sup>8</sup>כיא לוא מח̣שבותי מחשבותיכם ולוא דרכיכמה דרכי נואמ יהוה <sup>9</sup>כיא כגובה שמים מארץ כן גבהו דרכי מדרכיכמה ומחשבותי ממחשבותיכמה <sup>10</sup>כיא כאשר ירד הגשם והשלג מן השמים ושמה לוא ישוב כיא אמ הרוה את הארץ והולידה̣ והצמיחה ונתן זרע לזורע ולחם לאכול <sup>11</sup>כן יהיה דברי אש̣ר̣ יצא מפי לוא ישוב אלי ריקם כיא אמ עשה את אשר חפצתי והצליח את אשר שלחתיו <sup>12</sup>כיא בשמחה תצאו ובשלום תלכו ההרים והגבעות יפצחו לפניכמה רונה ו̣כול עצי השדה ימחוא כפ <sup>13</sup>תחת הנעצוץ יעלה בראוש ותחת הסרפוד יעלה אדס והיו ליהוה לאות ולשמ עולם לוא יכרת
translation.text: <sup>8</sup>For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD. <sup>9</sup>For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts. <sup>10</sup>For as the rain cometh down, and the snow from heaven, and returneth not thither, but watereth the earth, and maketh it bring forth and bud, that it may give seed to the sower, and bread to the eater: <sup>11</sup>So shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it. <sup>12</sup>For ye shall go out with joy, and be led forth with peace: the mountains and the hills shall break forth before you into singing, and all the trees of the field shall clap their hands. <sup>13</sup>Instead of the thorn shall come up the fir tree, and instead of the brier shall come up the myrtle tree: and it shall be to the LORD for a name, for an everlasting sign that shall not be cut off.
